verdict.rationale: Dynadot ships a first-party MCP server it markets as a way to manage domains just by talking to an AI assistant. The documented actions are a narrow set: availability checks, registration, viewing domains and account info, and reviewing nameservers and DNS. Natural-language operation also depends on an external AI assistant acting as the MCP client. Missing for 10: natural-language coverage of the broader 120+ API actions (DNS edits, transfers, renewals, aftermarket), in-depth setup and usage docs for the MCP, and independent or hands-on corroboration that it works.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands
